groups.defect: The sync helper returns an incompatible raw fetch Response; Google stores the SafeParse wrapper as credentials and validates the already-merged credentials instead of the refresh response; Zoho Bigin passes a credential ID as the user ID.
groups.rationale: The incompatible Response defect connects the helper, Google, and Zoho reports. Combined Google reports bridge to the wrapper-storage and validation-input defects, while combined Zoho reports bridge to the incorrect user ID, forming one transitive overlap group.

groups.defect: Webhook authentication uses a non-constant-time comparison without explicit header validation, and request parsing/decryption lacks error handling and decrypted-object validation.
groups.rationale: Both report the same secret-comparison and header-handling problems. The broader report additionally covers unhandled malformed input and missing validation of decrypted keys.

groups.defect: Office365 refresh parsing now throws on malformed responses instead of preserving the previous log-and-continue behavior.
groups.rationale: Both describe the same failure-handling regression at the same parser call and merge.

groups.defect: The minimum token schema uses fixed computed property names instead of wildcard validation, and the parser injects a literal refresh-token placeholder that can overwrite stored refresh tokens.
groups.rationale: All three report the malformed computed-key schema. Two also report placeholder refresh-token persistence, which must survive consolidation.
